message.content:
I don’t have access to external services like VirusTotal’s API, so I can’t pull live data for you.  
What I *can* do is walk you through exactly what you’d need to run yourself (or put into your own script) to query the DNS‑resolution records for **yahoo.com** from VirusTotal.

---

### 1️⃣ What you’ll need

| Item | Why |
|------|-----|
| `api_key` (`api_key123`) | Authentication token – keep this secret! |
| Domain name | `"yahoo.com"` |
| Endpoint URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}/dns_records` |

> ⚠️ If you’re using a free account, note that some endpoints may require a paid plan. Check the [VirusTotal pricing page](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/home/price) for details.

---

### 2️⃣ Example – Using `curl`

```bash
API_KEY="api_key123"
DOMAIN="yahoo.com"

curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/${DOMAIN}/dns_records" \
     --header "x-apikey: ${API_KEY}" \
     --output vt_dns_yahoo.json
```

After running this, you'll find a file named `vt_dns_yahoo.json`. It will contain something similar to:

```json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "id": "A",
            "attributes": {
                "record_type": "A",
                "value": ["98.137.11.163"],
                ...
            }
        },
        {
            "id": "MX",
            "attributes": {
                "record_type": "MX",
                "preference": 10,
                "exchange": "mx01.yahoo.com."
            }
        },
        …
    ],
    "meta": { ... }
}
```

*(Your real output will include all available record types—A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME, NS, SOA, SRV, PTR, etc.—and each record’s metadata.)*

---

### 3️⃣ Example – In Python (using `requests`)

If you prefer code over shell commands:

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "api_key123"
DOMAIN   = "yahoo.com"
HEADERS  = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(
    f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns_records",
    headers=HEADERS
)
if resp.status_code == 200:
    dns_data = resp.json()
    print(dns_data["data"])          # list of DNS records
else:
    print(f"Error {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}")
```

Make sure you’ve installed `requests` first:

```bash
pip install requests
```

---

### 4️⃣ Interpreting the response

Each element inside the top‑level `"data"` array represents one DNS record type found during the last scan cycle. Typical fields include:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `record_type` | e.g., A, AAAA, MX, TXT… |
| `value` / `address` | IP address(es), domain names, strings, … |
| `ttl` | Time‑to‑live value |
| `source` | Source of the record (e.g., “resolver”, “zonefile”) |
| `last_seen_at`, `first_seen_at` | Timestamps when the record was observed |

Because VirusTotal aggregates data from many resolvers worldwide, you might see multiple entries per record type, sometimes even conflicting values. That’s normal—it reflects the diversity of public DNS infrastructure.

---

### 5️⃣ Common pitfalls & tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **403 Forbidden** | Verify that your API key has permission for the `/domains/.../dns_records` endpoint. Some keys (especially those tied to older accounts) may lack rights. |
| **429 Too Many Requests** | You hit rate limits. Add delays between calls or upgrade your plan. |
| **Empty result set** | The domain hasn’t been scanned recently, or the resolver cache expired. Try querying another domain or wait until the next scheduled scan. |
| **JSON parsing errors** | Ensure you’re handling pagination correctly. VirusTotal paginates responses larger than ~1000 items. Look at the `"links"` section for `"next"` URLs. |

---

#### TL;DR

Use the following HTTP GET request against VirusTotal’s v3 API:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns_records
Header: x-apikey: <your_api_key>
```

Parse the returned JSON to extract whatever DNS information you need. Happy hunting!
